answer_1.quote: Furthermore, we extend our work to T5 encoder-decoder models and Arabic generative tasks. We pre-train two T5 small and base models for Arabic: AT5S and AT5B. AT5B achieves state-of-the-art results on several generative tasks by outperforming the recently proposed AraT5-base model both on automatic and human evaluations.

answer_2.quote: Specifically, we use ROUGE to evaluate models on the TS task and BLEU for QA, QG and EMD tasks.

answer_4.quote: The ideal way to measure performance on language generation tasks is to ask humans to evaluate the models' outputs. Thus, we evaluate our T5-based and AraB2B models on the three generation tasks of QG, EMD and TS using human annotators.
answer_4.guideline: We asked the annotators to label a hundred outputs from each model and each task for two scenarios: (1) Acceptable: each model output is labeled for whether it is acceptable (not strictly perfect) to the annotator or not, and (2) Best: where the annotator must pick exactly one best output out of the three ones.
